messages:
mika: flagging a perf regression after yesterday's selector tweak. host-side CPU and grpc small-write counts jumped. attaching quick profiler notes below.

amy: what was the selector change? new heuristics or a kernel add?

mika: selector started preferring micro-fused-attn for tokens <= 100 at 03:40. intent was latency reduction on short sequences but we're seeing host overhead increase.

jon: can you share the minimal flame summary? even a few hot stacks is fine.

mika: short flame (top stacks):
- preproc::tokenize -> token_norm::run -> kv_cache::lookup -> grpc_stream::emit_small -> syscall::writev
- http_ingress::frame -> small_write_path -> poll_write
KV miss rate up ~1.9x, small-write syscalls per request up 2.8x.

lina: there was also a batching-window shrink that landed in the autobatcher last week (shrink from 4ms->1ms) which increases more frequent sends for streaming clients. did that coincide?

mika: autobatch shrink is older. timeline: autobatch change (Feb 18), selector change (Mar 9). regression appeared within hours of selector rollout.

amy: hypothesis: micro-fused-attn reduces GPU decode time so host work (prefix/KV handling + streaming flushes) becomes the dominant fraction. More frequent small writes because the runtime no longer waits for larger batches.

jon: i ran a quick local bench. Setup: same instance type, model=large, mean seq ~85.
results:
- baseline selector: host CPU avg 29% p99 grpc 52ms small-writes/request 1.1
- micro-fused selector: host CPU avg 58% p99 grpc 118ms small-writes/request 3.2

mika: reproduce commands used:
```
./microbench --selector=baseline --clients=50 --seq=85 --n=2000 > base.log
./microbench --selector=micro-fused --clients=50 --seq=85 --n=2000 > fused.log
```

infra-bot: Canary deployment for selector v3 initiated at 03:40; automated metric guard tripped at 03:53, paused rollout.

lina: i can temporarily pin the selector in canary to baseline while we triage. also will toggle KV cache hot-sample size back to previous to see effect.

amy: we should also check batching heuristics interplay. if GPU time shrinks per request, batching decisions might now favor smaller per-batch sizes. we need to ensure prefix coalescing and KV prefetch don't regress.

jon: plan i'm running now:
- profile host syscall distribution between baseline and fused (30m)
- enable writev coalescing shim locally to see p99 impact (45m)
- verify kv cache working set with perf counters (20m)

mika: initial trace shows many tiny streaming frames (<256B) each triggering a writev. ingress shim currently writes frames as they arrive, no coalesce. adding a short coalesce window (200us) could merge 2-3 frames.

amy: downside: added latency for very low-latency paths. need opt-in per-route or per-client. could gate with a policy: coalesce if predicted decode remaining < X ms or if request uses KV-intensive prefixes.

lina: i pushed an override to canary to pin selector->baseline and revert kv hot-sample change. monitoring says kv miss returned to baseline within 3 mins.

infra-bot: Canary override applied at 04:10 successfully.

jon: quick results from writev-coalesce shim run (local cluster): fused selector + shim -> host CPU drop from 58% to 34%, p99 grpc from 118ms to 60ms, small-writes/request down from 3.2 to 1.3. shim increases avg write latency by ~60us but overall request p99 improves.

amy: promising. can we roll the shim to canary before re-enabling the selector change? also need to add heuristic to avoid coalesce for long-stream interactive sessions where we care about per-token latency.

mika: agreed. action items: 
- jon: open PR with writev-coalesce-shim + perf tests (target: 4h)
- lina: keep selector pinned in canary until shim lands (in progress)
- amy + mika: add selector guard to disallow micro-fused-attn for requests with >X prefix tokens or high kv-touch ratios (next-day)
- jon: run full perf matrix (various seq distributions, streaming and non-streaming) and post numbers to thread (6h)

lina: canary metrics look stable with selector pinned. continuing to monitor.

amy: note for postmortem: we should treat kernel selection changes as a system-level perf experiment (not GPU-only). need end-to-end profiling checklist: host syscall distribution, batching-change effects, kv working-set, streaming write patterns.

mika: will draft a short checklist and the perf artifact bundle (bench runs, flamegraphs, syscall histograms). linking PR when ready.

infra-bot: Reminder: metric alerting suppressed for this canary for 30m as part of triage window.
